get.summary: Scaffold route, left public so you can check the server is up without a token.

post.summary:
`POST /auth/login`: exchanges an email and password for an access token.

`@Body()` hands over the request body as a `LoginDto`; Nest validates it first and
answers `400` itself if it is invalid. `@HttpCode(200)` is needed because Nest
answers `201 Created` to every POST by default, and a login creates nothing.

get.summary:
`GET /auth/me`: returns the user the token belongs to. The frontend calls it when the
page loads to check that a stored token is still valid and to learn who is logged in.

It has no `@Public()`, so JwtAuthGuard requires a valid token before this runs.
`@Roles` opens it to drivers too (routes are admin-only by default), and it works before
a forced password change, so the frontend can learn that the change is required.

post.summary:
`POST /auth/verify-email`: confirms the email address from the token in the welcome
email's link. Public: the driver cannot log in before this. `204` on success.

`POST /auth/change-password`: the logged-in user replaces their password. This is the
one action allowed while a temporary password must be changed. Returns the updated user.

requestBody.description: The website's application JSON (snake_case fields, values mostly strings). Required: request_id, first_name, last_name, email, phone. Other fields are kept as sent.

post.summary:
`POST /applications`: receives a driver application from the gonzocar.com form.

Public: applicants have no account. The body is typed `unknown` instead of a DTO class,
so the global ValidationPipe leaves it alone and ApplicationsService does the (lenient)
checks. Answers `201` with the same body for a new or a repeated submission.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only applications with this status. Omit for all.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day to include, e.g. `2026-10-01`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day to include, e.g. `2026-10-15` (the whole day counts).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Text to look for; which fields are searched depends on the list. Case does not matter.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page (1 to 100).

get.summary:
`GET /applications`: one page of applications, newest first.

`@Query()` collects the query string into the DTO and validates it, the same way
`@Body()` does for a request body. An invalid value (e.g. `status=foo`) is a `400`.

capital.description: Required, as an amount in USD, only when has_startup_funds is no

post.summary:
`POST /applications/manual`: an admin types in an application by hand, with its documents (D68). Same fields and
rules as the website form; the result is an ordinary application that is then approved like any other. Admin
only (no `@Public`). Multipart form data: the text fields plus the files `license_file` (required),
`rating_file` and `earnings_file` (JPG, PNG or PDF, at most 10 MB each). The file fields end in `_file` because
`earnings` is already a text field (weekly earnings).

The interceptor is multer, the library you would mount as `upload.fields([...])` in Express: it reads the
multipart body, keeps the files in memory and leaves the text fields in `@Body()`, where the global
ValidationPipe checks them against `ManualApplicationDto`.

`201` with `created: false` when the same `request_id` was already stored.

`POST /applications/bulk-delete`: deletes applications for good, with their documents and (when no one else
uses the phone) their text history (B66). All or nothing: `409` if any is approved, and then nothing is
deleted. Unknown ids are ignored.

POST with a body rather than DELETE: a DELETE request with a body is poorly supported by proxies and HTTP
clients. Declared before `:id` routes so "bulk-delete" is never read as an id (it is also a POST, so it
could not clash with `GET :id` anyway).

get.summary:
`GET /applications/:id`: one application with its full details.

`ParseUUIDPipe` rejects an id that is not a UUID with `400` before any query runs
(Postgres would otherwise fail on it with a 500). A valid but unknown id is a `404`.

post.summary:
`POST /applications/:id/approve`: creates the driver and marks the application approved, and texts the
applicant. Optional body `{ "message": "..." }` is the approval text the admin picked and edited (B81); without
it the first approved template is sent. `400` for an unknown placeholder in it.

POST because it is an action with side effects, not an edit of a field. `@HttpCode(200)`
because it returns the updated application rather than creating a resource at this URL.

`POST /applications/:id/reject`: declines the application (shown as "Declined", B69). No driver is created.
Optional body `{ "message": "..." }` texts the applicant that declined text, as the admin picked and edited
it (B72, B81); without a message nothing is sent. `503` if the text could not be sent (then nothing is declined).
`POST /applications/:id/hold`: puts the application on hold to decide later.

get.summary: `GET /applications/:id/documents`: the files, as our own copies (D54) or admin uploads (D68).

put.summary:
`PUT /applications/:id/documents/:kind`: puts one file (multipart field `file`) in the licence, rating or earnings
slot, replacing what is there, a website copy included (D68). JPG, PNG or PDF, at most 10 MB; `400` otherwise.
Returns the slot. PUT because the slot ends up holding exactly this file however many times it is sent.

`POST /sms/:kind/:id/messages`: sends a text, according to SMS_MODE.
`409` texting is off, `502` Quo refused (the failure is saved and shown in the chat),
`400` the application's phone is not a US number, `404` unknown record.
`POST /sms/:kind/:id/sync`: pulls this contact's history from Quo (texts sent from the Quo app too).

`GET /message-templates`: every template, grouped by kind, with its placeholders and last edit.

post.summary: `POST /message-templates`: adds a template. `400` empty, too long or unknown placeholder; `409` name taken.

put.summary:
`PUT /message-templates/:id`: replaces a template's name and text. PUT because both are replaced. `400` empty,
too long or unknown placeholder; `404` unknown id; `409` name taken.

delete.summary: `DELETE /message-templates/:id`: `404` unknown id; `409` if it is the last template of its kind.

get.summary: `GET /ledger-presets`: every preset, charges first, each kind in the order of its cards.

post.summary: `POST /ledger-presets`: adds a preset at the end of its kind. `400` bad amount or text; `409` name taken.

put.summary:
`PUT /ledger-presets/order`: sets the order of one kind's cards (`kind`, `ids` = all that kind's ids). `400` the ids
are not exactly that kind's presets. Declared before `:id` so "order" is never read as an id.

`PUT /ledger-presets/:id`: replaces a preset's name, amount and description (PUT because all three are replaced; the
amount may be null). `400` bad amount or text; `404` unknown id; `409` name taken.

delete.summary: `DELETE /ledger-presets/:id`: `404` unknown id. Entries made from it keep their text and amount.

`GET /drivers/:id`: one driver. `400` for a malformed id, `404` if unknown.

post.summary:
`POST /drivers/:id/onboarding`: ticks or un-ticks one onboarding step (D56). The driver becomes `active` when
the third step is ticked, and goes back to `onboarding` when one is un-ticked. Returns the updated driver.
`409` if the driver is inactive.

`POST /drivers/:id/aliases`: adds a payment alias (a name or handle the driver pays from, per payment method) so
their payments match automatically (D69). `409` with the owner's name when another driver already has it.
Returns the updated driver.

delete.summary: `DELETE /drivers/:id/aliases/:aliasId`: removes one of the driver's aliases. Returns the updated driver.

post.summary: `POST /drivers/:id/deactivate`: the driver left (B67). Their login stops working at once.
`POST /drivers/:id/reactivate`: back to `active` (all steps done) or `onboarding`; login works again.

get.summary: `GET /payments`: one page of payments, most recent first. `?match=review` lists "Needs review".

post.summary:
`POST /payments/manual`: records a payment an admin received by hand (cash, check, card, or any method) and
credits the driver's ledger. `201` the payment (also when the same `requestKey` is sent again); `400` bad
amount or date, unknown driver; `409` a possible duplicate (body has `code: "possible_duplicate"` and the
payment found; send `confirmDuplicate: true` to record anyway), the key reused, or the reference used before.

`POST /payments/:id/void`: voids a payment recorded by hand and reverses its ledger credit. `201` the payment;
`404` unknown payment; `409` not a manual payment, or already voided.

`POST /payments/:id/assign`: assigns or re-assigns a payment to a driver and saves the payer's name as
that driver's alias (unless another driver already owns it, which the answer reports).
`404` unknown payment, `400` unknown driver, `409` a rejected or discrepancy payment.

`GET /drivers/:id/ledger/overview`: the balance, what is owed by age of the charges (0–6, 7–13, 14–29, 30+ days)
and the newest confirmed payment. `404` unknown driver.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day to cover, `YYYY-MM-DD` (its whole week or month is included). Default: 11 periods before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day to cover, `YYYY-MM-DD` (its whole week or month is included). Default: today in Chicago.

get.summary:
`GET /drivers/:id/ledger/summary?period=week|month`: totals per week (Monday to Sunday) or month, newest
first, empty periods included. `400` bad dates or more than 104 periods; `404` unknown driver.

`GET /drivers/:id/ledger/entries/:entryId`: one entry with what it reverses or was reversed by, the charge it
is applied against, the credits applied against it and its payment. `404` no such entry on this driver.

post.summary:
`POST /drivers/:id/ledger/entries`: adds a manual charge or credit (late fee, flat tire, discount, …), or a
credit applied against a charge (`appliesToId`). `201` the entry (also when the same `requestKey` is sent
again); `400` invalid amount, date or direction, or more than is left on the charge; `404` unknown driver or
charge; `409` the key reused for a different entry.

info.title: GonzoCar API
info.description: Admin and driver API for the GonzoCar platform.

password.description: The account's password, in plain text (it only travels over HTTPS in production).

mustChangePassword.description:
True while the user still has a system-generated password. Until they change it, every
endpoint except `GET /auth/me` and `POST /auth/change-password` answers `403`.

accessToken.description: Signed token the client sends back on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

token.description: The `token` from the verification link in the welcome email.

currentPassword.description: The password the user logs in with now (the temporary one, at first login).

newPassword.description:
The new password: at least 8 characters. The 72-byte limit (bcrypt) is checked by the
service, since characters outside English can take more than one byte.

application_id.description: Our id for the application. A repeated submission (same `request_id`) gets the same id.

created.description: False when the same `request_id` had already been stored (a double click or a retry): nothing new was made.

phone.description: As the applicant typed it (usually 10 digits).

submittedAt.description: When the applicant pressed submit, by their browser's clock.

alertError.description: Why the alert text to staff about this application could not be sent; null if it did not fail.

total.description: Number of applications matching the filter, across all pages.

ids.description: The applications to delete. Ids that no longer exist are ignored.

filesNotRemoved.description:
Copied files (documents, texted-in files) that could not be removed from the bucket. The database rows are
gone either way; the reason for each is in the server log. 0 when everything was removed.

phone.description: As the applicant typed it (usually 10 digits).

submittedAt.description: When the applicant pressed submit, by their browser's clock.

alertError.description: Why the alert text to staff about this application could not be sent; null if it did not fail.

requestId.description: The website's id for the submission.

licenseStoragePath.description: Paths in the client's Supabase `driver-documents` bucket.

payload.description: The full submission as the website sent it, minus the bot-check token.

reviewedById.description: The admin who last reviewed it. Null while pending.

driverId.description: The driver created on approval. Null unless approved.

alertedAt.description: When the alert text to staff was really sent; null if it was not (off, dry run, or failed).

createdBy.description: The admin who added it by hand (D68). Null for applications that came from the website form.

message.description:
The text, with `{firstName}` / `{lastName}` placeholders (filled in by the API; unknown ones are refused, 400).
1 to 1000 characters after trimming. Approve without it sends the first approved template; decline without it
sends no text.

kind.description: Which upload on the form: licence, rating screenshot or earnings screenshot.

status.description: `stored`: our copy can be opened; `pending`: still being copied; `failed`: it cannot be copied (see `error`).

origin.description: `website`: copied from the website's storage; `admin`: uploaded by an admin (D68).

contentType.description: MIME type, e.g. `image/png`; null if unknown.

url.description: Short-lived link (about 10 minutes) to open our copy. Null unless `stored`.

error.description: Why it could not be copied, in plain words. Null if it did not fail.

uploadedByEmail.description: The admin who uploaded it (admin uploads only; also null if that account was removed).

sourceConnected.description: Whether the website's document function is connected (`DOCUMENTS_SOURCE_*`); without it nothing can be copied.

storageConnected.description: Whether our file bucket is connected (`S3_*`); without it nothing can be stored.

authorId.description: The admin who wrote it; null if that account was removed since.

authorEmail.description: The author's email, shown as their name (admins have no name field). Null if the account was removed.

total.description: All notes of the application, across pages.

body.description:
The note, 1 to 2000 characters after trimming; line breaks are kept. `@Transform` trims it before the checks, so
a note of only spaces is refused (400) instead of saved empty.

mode.description: `off`: sending refused. `dry_run`: texts are saved, not sent. `live`: really sent.

quoConfigured.description: Whether the Quo API key and number are set, which syncing the history needs.

filesConfigured.description: Whether the file bucket is set; without it files stay pending.

contentType.description: MIME type, e.g. `image/jpeg`; null if unknown.

status.description: `stored` files can be opened; `pending` ones are still being copied; `failed` ones never will be.

url.description: Short-lived link to open the file (about 10 minutes). Null unless `stored`.

body.description: The words; empty for a text that is only a file.

mode.description: Null for inbound texts. `dry_run` texts were never sent.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did.

sentByEmail.description: The admin who sent it from this app; null for inbound texts and texts sent from the Quo app.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `before` to get the next, older page. Null when there is nothing older.

contactPhone.description: The contact's number the chat is with (E.164).

contactPhoneProblem.description: Why no text can be sent to this number (for example it cannot exist in the US); null when it can.

text.description: The words to send, 1 to 1600 characters (Quo's limit). Plain text only: Quo's API cannot send files.

added.description: Of those, how many were new to us.

contentType.description: MIME type, e.g. `image/jpeg`; null if unknown.

status.description: `stored` files can be opened; `pending` ones are still being copied; `failed` ones never will be.

url.description: Short-lived link to open the file (about 10 minutes). Null unless `stored`.

direction.description: Who sent it: `inbound` = the contact texted it to us.

name.description: The label in the dropdown, e.g. "No valid licence".

body.description: The text with its placeholders, e.g. `Hi {firstName}, ...`.

placeholders.description: The placeholders this template may use, e.g. `["firstName", "lastName"]`.

updatedByEmail.description: Email of the admin who last edited it; null for the default text (or a removed account).

name.description: 1 to 60 characters after trimming. Two templates of a kind cannot share a name (409).

body.description: The new text, 1 to 1000 characters after trimming; line breaks kept. Unknown placeholders are refused (400).

name.description: 1 to 60 characters after trimming. Two templates of a kind cannot share a name (409).

body.description: The new text, 1 to 1000 characters after trimming; line breaks kept. Unknown placeholders are refused (400).

amountCents.description: The default amount in whole cents, or null for "enter amount".

description.description: What the Description box is filled with.

position.description: The order of the cards within a kind, from 1.

name.description: 1 to 60 characters after trimming. Two presets of a kind cannot share a name (409).

amountCents.description: Whole cents, 1 to 1,000,000 ($10,000), or left out / null for "enter amount".

description.description: What the Description box is filled with: 1 to 500 characters after trimming.

ids.description: Exactly the ids of that kind's presets, each once (400 otherwise).

name.description: 1 to 60 characters after trimming. Two presets of a kind cannot share a name (409).

amountCents.description: Whole cents, 1 to 1,000,000 ($10,000), or left out / null for "enter amount".

description.description: What the Description box is filled with: 1 to 500 characters after trimming.

value.description: As entered or as the provider wrote it.

source.description: Imported from the old system, learned from a confident AI match, or entered by an admin.

status.description: `onboarding` until all three steps are done, then `active`; `inactive` when the driver left (D56).

createdAt.description: When the driver was created (the application's approval).

aliases.description: Every payment alias of the driver, grouped by payment method then by value. Empty if none yet.

paymentCount.description: Number of payments assigned to this driver.

lastPaymentAt.description: When the driver's most recent payment happened; null if none.

balanceCents.description: Ledger balance in cents: credits minus debits (D60). Negative = the driver owes money; 0 with no entries.

total.description: Number of drivers matching the filter, across all pages.

done.description: `true` marks the step done (now, by the admin); `false` clears it.

type.description: The payment method the name or handle belongs to; matching only compares aliases of the payment's own method.

value.description: The name, handle, company, email or phone as the payer shows it. Extra spaces are trimmed.

receivedAt.description: When our mail server received it.

statusReason.description: Why it was rejected or failed (always set for those statuses).

authDkimPass.description: True only when DKIM passed for the provider's own domain.

authDkimDomain.description: The signing domain that passed, e.g. `venmo.com`.

imapUid.description: The message's UID in the mailbox (for finding it in Gmail by hand if needed).

paymentId.description: The payment this email created, if any.

total.description: Number of emails matching the filters, across all pages.

PaymentManualMethod.description: For a payment an admin recorded by hand: how it was paid (cash, check, ...). Null for every other source.

manualMethod.description: For a payment an admin recorded by hand: how it was paid (cash, check, ...). Null for every other source.

description.description: For a payment an admin recorded by hand: the text they gave for the driver's statement.

internalNote.description: For a payment an admin recorded by hand: their staff-only note.

amountCents.description: Integer cents. The frontend formats it; never a float.

senderName.description: The payer's name exactly as the provider wrote it.

transactionId.description: The provider's transaction id, when the email showed one.

occurredAt.description: When the payment happened (exact time from the email, or when the email arrived).

extractionConfidence.description: How sure the AI was about what it read from the email, 0 to 1. Null for sources without AI.

externalId.description: The record it came from; for email sources, the id of the inbound email.

driver.description: The driver it is assigned to. Null while unmatched.

suggestedDriver.description: The AI's best guess when it was not sure enough: "Needs review".

matchMethod.description: How it was assigned: alias, exact name, AI or by an admin.

matchConfidence.description: 1 for alias and name, the AI's confidence for AI matches and suggestions, null for manual.

matchExplanation.description: One line on why (the alias, the AI's reason, or why matching failed).

total.description: Number of payments matching the filters, across all pages.

method.description: How it was paid. Zelle, Cash App, Venmo, Stripe and Chime payments normally arrive by email by themselves.

paidOn.description: The day it was paid, `YYYY-MM-DD` in Chicago: today or up to 90 days back.

reference.description:
A receipt number, check number or confirmation code, if there is one. Two manual payments cannot share the same
reference (a check recorded twice is refused).

requestKey.description:
A UUID the form makes once per payment. Sending the same request again (a double click, a retry) returns the
payment already recorded instead of recording a second one.

confirmDuplicate.description:
Set to true to record it although the driver already has a confirmed payment of the same amount within three
days (the answer to the "possible duplicate" warning).

description.description:
The text for the driver's statement. Empty: the ledger writes its own ("Cash payment · ref 17"). Up to 500
characters.

internalNote.description: A note for staff only (optional, up to 500 characters). Typed once; copied to the ledger credit; never on a statement.

reason.description: Why the payment is voided, e.g. "Check bounced". 1 to 400 characters after trimming.

driverId.description: The driver the payment belongs to.

aliasSaved.description: True if the payer's name was saved as a new alias of the driver.

aliasOwnedBy.description:
The driver who already owns the payer's name as an alias, if it is someone else: that alias is NOT
moved (one alias, one driver); the admin decides.

PaymentSource.description: For a payment row: where the payment came from.

paymentSource.description: For a payment row: where the payment came from.

paymentManualMethod.description: For a payment row recorded by hand: how it was paid.

runningBalanceCents.description: Balance after this entry, in date order (credits minus debits; negative = owes).

appliesToRef.description: The reference of the charge this credit is applied against.

reversalOfRef.description: The reference of the entry this reversal cancels.

reversedByRef.description: The reference of the reversal that cancelled this entry.

canVoidPayment.description: For a payment row recorded by hand and still confirmed: it can be voided.

creditableCents.description:
For a charge that can still be credited against: how much of it is left (its amount minus the active credits
applied to it). Null when it cannot (not a charge, reversed, or already fully credited).

entryNo.description: The short number people use, e.g. 1042 in "CH-1042".

effectiveDate.description: The Chicago day it belongs to, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

reversalOfId.description: The entry this one cancels (reversals only).

appliesToId.description: The charge this credit is applied against, if any.

internalNote.description: The staff-only note typed with the entry, if any.

reversedById.description: The reversal that cancelled this entry, if any.

canReverse.description: True when an admin may reverse it here: not a reversal, not a payment credit, not reversed already.

createdById.description: Null for entries made by the system (payment credits from matching).

createdAt.description: When it was recorded (may be later than `effectiveDate`).

debitCents.description: Sum of the debits (charges) among them.

creditCents.description: Sum of the credits among them (payments, credits, and reversals of charges).

total.description: Entries that match the filters, across pages.

balanceCents.description: The driver's balance now (credits minus debits; negative = owes), whatever the filters.

balanceBeforeCents.description:
Balance at the start of the `from` day: every entry dated before it. Null when no `from` was given. A statement
starts from it.

pastDueCents.description: Everything 7 days old or more (the three numbers above it).

balanceCents.description: Credits minus debits; negative = the driver owes.

asOf.description: The Chicago day the ages are counted to, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

start.description: First day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (a Monday for weeks, the 1st for months).

chargesCents.description: Charges (rent and manual charges, incl. a debit opening balance).

creditsCents.description: Manual credits (discounts, goodwill, a credit opening balance).

reversalsCents.description: Net effect of reversals made in the period: positive gives money back to the driver, negative takes it.

closingCents.description: Balance at the end of the period.

entryNo.description: The short number people use, e.g. 1042 in "CH-1042".

effectiveDate.description: The Chicago day it belongs to, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

reversalOfId.description: The entry this one cancels (reversals only).

appliesToId.description: The charge this credit is applied against, if any.

internalNote.description: The staff-only note typed with the entry, if any.

reversedById.description: The reversal that cancelled this entry, if any.

canReverse.description: True when an admin may reverse it here: not a reversal, not a payment credit, not reversed already.

createdById.description: Null for entries made by the system (payment credits from matching).

createdAt.description: When it was recorded (may be later than `effectiveDate`).

transactionId.description: The provider's transaction id, or the reference typed for a manual payment.

reversalOf.description: For a reversal: the entry it cancels.

reversedBy.description: The reversal that cancelled this entry.

appliesTo.description: For a credit: the charge it is applied against.

appliedCredits.description: For a charge: the credits applied against it, oldest first.

payment.description: For a payment entry: the payment.

creditableCents.description: For a charge: how much of it can still be credited, or null.

canVoidPayment.description: For a payment entry recorded by hand and still confirmed: it can be voided.

direction.description:
`debit`: a charge, the driver owes more (late fee, flat tire, damage, toll…). `credit`: the driver owes less
(a discount, money handed back…). What it was for goes in `reason` (D61).

amountCents.description: Whole cents, 1 to 1,000,000 ($10,000). Always positive: `direction` says which way it goes.

effectiveDate.description: The day the charge or credit belongs to, `YYYY-MM-DD` in Chicago: today or up to 90 days back.

reason.description: Why, e.g. "Flat tire, rear left, replaced at Discount Tire". 1 to 500 characters after trimming.

requestKey.description:
A UUID the form makes once per entry. Sending the same request again (a double click, a retry after a timeout)
returns the entry already made instead of making a second one.

appliesToId.description:
"Credit against this charge": the charge this credit reduces (e.g. a waived late fee). Only a credit can name
one, the charge must be on this driver and not reversed, and the amount can be at most what is left on it.

internalNote.description: A note for staff only (optional, up to 500 characters). Typed once, never changed, never printed on a statement.

reason.description: Why the entry is cancelled, e.g. "Late fee waived by the owner". 1 to 400 characters after trimming.
